art_instructions: Medium, eye-level view inside the same cozy classroom as the previous page: soft blue walls, a sunlit window at back right, honey‑oak low desk and chair on a small woven geometric rug. Owl (small, chibi proportions; mottled brown‑and‑cream feathers; round amber eyes; green scarf) sits upright at the same low desk; her tiny satchel hangs from the chair back. She smiles with focused concentration: her left wing points to neat groups of smooth pebbles on the left side of the desk (arranged in small piles to suggest counting), and two chunky wooden dice nearby show only pips (no numerals). With her right wing she traces a gentle curve in a shallow sand tray centered on the desk to suggest practicing letter shapes. On the right side of the desk sits a small abacus with red, yellow, and green beads, and a wooden puzzle board with removable “letter‑like” pieces made of simple curves and angles; angle them so no actual alphabet characters are readable. Behind Owl, a short chalkboard easel shows only simple lines, dots, and basic shapes (circles/triangles) to imply learning; absolutely no text or digits anywhere. Keep the palette pastel and airy, with the green scarf and a few red abacus beads as accents; diffuse daylight fills the room. Owl occupies about one third of the frame; the desk fills the lower half; objects are arranged left‑to‑right (pebbles, sand tray, abacus/puzzle) for clear storytelling. Do not include any readable letters or numbers; use dots, shapes, and abstract squiggles only.
